docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The ITS-FMS Interface is a standard for communication between logistics IT-suppliers (FMS) wanting to integrate Intelligent Transport Systems services and ITS Cloud Service Providers (CSP) that offer the required services. These services consist of real-time traffic and infrastructure events that are relevant on the current route of a truck.

The interface is an implementation of the Open Trip Model 5.0, an open standard for communication about logistics and traffic. It has been developed with and already implemented by several market companies with support of the Dutch government. All certified Cloud Service Providers that have access to the relevant data provide their services following this standard.

The main goal is to make implementation of these services as easy as possible for all software suppliers in the logistics market, to make traffic flow more smooth, predictable and safe for everyone.

docs.title: Scope and objective
docs.text:
With the ITS-FMS interface, a set of C-ITS use cases, based on the use cases defined by the Talking Traffic project, are linked to logistics IT-systems (such as Fleet Management Systems), with a specific focus towards logistics operators.

The following use cases are currently supported:

  • Traffic light status and timing information from intelligent traffic light controllers (iVRI)
  • Priority allocation at iVRIs
  • Lane configuration and variable message sign information
  • Early warning messages from approaching emergency vehicles
  • Dynamic location update frequency control

Additional use cases are defined in the Protobuf specification and may become available in future versions. See Event codes for the full list.

This set of applications is characterized by low-latency services that make use of cellular communication services.

docs.title: Target group
docs.text: This document is intended for logistics IT-suppliers wanting to integrate ITS services. The document is a technical key specification for the connection between Fleet Management Systems and our platform.

docs.title: High level architecture
docs.text:
The interface consists of two types of communication:

  • REST API (JSON over HTTPS) - For static data: vehicle and route information, based on the Open Trip Model
  • WebSocket (Protocol Buffers over WSS) - For dynamic data: real-time location updates, ITS events, control messages, and time synchronization

There are multiple implementation options for FMS systems:

  1. Backend-to-backend - All communication goes through the FMS backend
  2. Direct to vehicle - Communication goes directly from the on-board unit to us
  3. Hybrid - REST API via the backend, WebSocket directly from the vehicle

docs.title: Interface flow
docs.text:
The following steps describe the typical flow for connecting to our platform:

  1. Announce vehicle - Register the vehicle using the REST API (PUT /vehicles)
  2. Announce route - Register the route using the REST API (PUT /routes) - required when iVRI priority is enabled
  3. Open WebSocket - Open one WebSocket connection per vehicle over WSS
  4. Send location updates - Start communication by sending location updates in Protobuf over the WebSocket
  5. Respond to time sync - Respond to timestamp requests to keep the connection open, and keep sending location updates
  6. Receive events - Receive real-time ITS event messages

Inactivity timeout

If no activity is detected on an open WebSocket during 5 minutes, the connection will be closed.

docs.title: Bearer token
docs.text:
All API requests (REST and WebSocket) must include a Bearer token for authentication. SSL (TLS) is used to encrypt all in-flight data.

The token must be included in the Authorization header of every HTTP request:

Authorization: Bearer <api_key>

For the WebSocket connection, the same API key is used during the connection handshake.

docs.title: Obtaining an API key
docs.text:
An API key will be provided after the onboarding process is complete. Contact support to initiate onboarding and receive credentials for both the REST API and WebSocket interfaces.

After onboarding you will receive:

  • A unique API key (used as Bearer token)
  • A base URL for the REST API endpoints ({baseUrl}/vehicles, {baseUrl}/routes)
  • A WebSocket URL for real-time communication ({baseUrl}/ws)

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text: The authorization of FMS parties to subscribe to ITS services is not part of this technical specification. Authorization is described in a separate bilateral contract.

docs.title: Event codes
docs.text: Each ITS use case is identified by an ITSEventCode. These codes identify the type of event and determine which fields are filled in the Protobuf message.

docs.title: Currently supported
docs.text:
The following event codes are currently supported:

Code Name Description 001 CHANGED_FREQUENCY_REQUEST CSP requests the FMS to change the location update frequency to X Hz 104 LANE_CONFIGURATION Lane configuration changed (variable message signs) 301 PRIORITY iVRI priority status update 401 TRAFFIC_LIGHT_STATUS Traffic light status update 402 TRAFFIC_LIGHT_TIMING Time to green / time to red 209 EMERGENCY_VEHICLE_APPROACHING Approaching emergency services (early warning)

In addition to event codes, the following message types are supported:

Message type Description LOCATION_UPDATE Vehicle position updates (FMS → CSP) TIMESTAMP_MESSAGE Time synchronization (bidirectional) ERROR_MESSAGE Error notifications (CSP → FMS)

docs.title: Defined in specification (not yet available)
docs.text: The following event codes are defined in the Protobuf specification but are not yet supported. They may become available in a future version.

docs.title: Signaling and speed advice
docs.text: Code Name Description 101 MAXIMUM_SPEED Maximum allowed speed of X km/h 102 ADVISORY_SPEED_LIMIT Advised speed of X km/h 103 OVERTAKING_BAN Overtaking prohibited

docs.title: Dangerous situations
docs.text: Code Name Description 201 ROAD_WORKS Road works ahead 202 EVENTS Event ahead 203 PLACEHOLDER Rail level crossings (placeholder) 204 TRAFFIC_JAM Traffic jam ahead 205 STATIONARY_VEHICLE Stationary vehicle ahead 206 INCIDENT Incident ahead 207 WEATHER_CONDITIONS Bad weather conditions ahead 208 OBJECTS_ON_ROAD Objects/cargo on the road 210 ROAD_INSPECTOR Road inspector on the road 211 BRIDGE_OPENING Open bridge ahead 212 GHOST_DRIVER_WARNING Ghost driver approaching

docs.title: iVRI
docs.text: Code Name Description 302 SELECTIVE_ACCESS Selective access systems (placeholder) 403 ADVISORY_SPEED Traffic light optimal speed advice 404 RAIL_CROSSING_STATUS Rail level crossing time to open (placeholder) 410 TRAFFIC_LIGHT_INFO Additional traffic light info

docs.title: Sensor data
docs.text: Code Name Description 501 TIRE_PRESSURE_GAUGE Tire pressure information 502 ALTIMETER Vehicle height information 503 WEIGHT Vehicle weight information 504 PARKING_OCCUPATION Parking / loading area occupation (placeholder) 505 PARKING_RESERVATION Parking / loading area reservation (placeholder) 506 WILDLIFE_CROSSING Animals crossing the road

docs.title: Other
docs.text: Code Name Description 601 RESTRICTED_ACCESS Zone with restricted access

docs.title: Protocol Buffers specification
docs.text:
The WebSocket interface uses Protocol Buffers (proto3) for message encoding. The proto specification defines all message types exchanged between FMS and CSP over the WebSocket connection.

Download the specification: FMS_ITS_Interface_Specification.proto

docs.title: Envelope message
docs.text:
All communication uses a single envelope message:

message FmsItsMessage {
  MessageType     message_type = 1;
  string          vehicle_id = 2;
  FmsItsContainer container = 3;
}

docs.title: Container
docs.text:
The container holds the actual message payload. Depending on the message_type, different fields are populated:

message FmsItsContainer {
  TimestampMessage    timestamp_message = 1;  // TIMESTAMP_MESSAGE
  InfoContainer       info_container = 2;     // EVENT_MESSAGE
  ContentContainer    content_container = 3;  // EVENT_MESSAGE
  LocationUpdateEvent location_update = 4;    // LOCATION_UPDATE
  ErrorMessage        error_message = 5;      // ERROR_MESSAGE
}

docs.title: Message types
docs.text:
enum MessageType {
  MESSAGETYPE_UNKNOWN = 0;
  TIMESTAMP_MESSAGE = 1;
  LOCATION_UPDATE = 2;
  EVENT_MESSAGE = 3;
  ERROR_MESSAGE = 4;
}

docs.title: Location update
docs.text:
Sent from FMS to CSP with current vehicle position information.

message LocationUpdateEvent {
  string                    id = 1;             // Unique ID for this update
  google.protobuf.Timestamp creation_date = 2;  // GPS fix timestamp (UTC)
  GeoReference              geo_reference = 3;  // Lat/lon position
  MeasurementType           speed = 4;          // Vehicle speed
  MeasurementType           heading = 5;        // Vehicle heading
  LifeCycle                 lifecycle = 6;      // Must be ACTUAL
  google.protobuf.Timestamp device_date = 7;    // Device clock timestamp
  float                     gps_quality = 8;    // Deviation in meters (95%)
}

The GeoReference only supports LAT_LON_POINT_GEO_REFERENCE:

message GeoReference {
  double           lat = 1;
  double           lon = 2;
  GeoReferenceType type = 3;
}

docs.title: Timestamp message
docs.text:
Used for time synchronization between FMS and CSP.

message TimestampMessage {
  google.protobuf.Timestamp request_transmission = 1;   // Set by CSP
  google.protobuf.Timestamp request_reception = 2;      // Set by FMS on receipt
  google.protobuf.Timestamp response_transmission = 3;  // Set by FMS on send
}

docs.title: Event message
docs.text: ITS events are sent from CSP to FMS and consist of two containers:

docs.title: Info container
docs.text:
General metadata about the event:

message InfoContainer {
  string                    author = 1;           // CSP that created the message
  string                    event_id = 2;         // Unique event ID (unique per CSP)
  MessageType               message_type = 3;     // NEW, UPDATE, or DELETE
  int32                     event_version = 4;    // Version of this event
  google.protobuf.Timestamp creation_time = 5;    // Time of sending (UTC)
  int32                     desired_interval = 6; // Requested GPS sample rate (seconds)
}

docs.title: Content container
docs.text:
The actual event data:

message ContentContainer {
  ItsEventCode its_event_code = 1;  // Event type identifier
  EventInfo    event_info = 2;      // Event details
}

docs.title: Event info
docs.text:
message EventInfo {
  string               event_text = 1;              // Textual description
  Location             location = 2;                // Event location (EPSG:4326)
  StaticEventMetadata  static_event_metadata = 3;   // For static events
  DynamicEventMetadata dynamic_event_metadata = 4;  // For dynamic events
}

docs.title: Static event metadata
docs.text:
Contains specific data depending on the event code. Currently supported fields:

Field Applicable event codes road_configuration LANE_CONFIGURATION ivri_container TRAFFIC_LIGHT_STATUS, TRAFFIC_LIGHT_TIMING, PRIORITY lane_info LANE_CONFIGURATION, TRAFFIC_LIGHT_STATUS, TRAFFIC_LIGHT_TIMING

docs.title: Road configuration
docs.text:
message RoadConfiguration {
  RoadConfigStatus   road_config_status = 1;    // Lane status
  MeasurementType    max_speed = 2;             // Speed if CHANGED_MAX_SPEED
  RoadConfigLocation road_config_location = 3;  // UPSTREAM or DOWNSTREAM
  bool               flashing = 4;              // Flashing lights present
  bool               red_border = 5;            // Red border present
}

Road configuration status values:

Status Description OPEN Open (falling green arrow) CLOSED / CLOSED_FOR_ALL_TRAFFIC Closed for all traffic (red cross) MERGE_RIGHT Merge right MERGE_LEFT Merge left END_OF_RESTRICTIONS End of restrictions CLOSED_FOR_YOU Closed for your vehicle type CHANGED_MAX_SPEED Temporary speed change BLANK Variable message sign is off

docs.title: iVRI container
docs.text:
message IvriContainer {
  PriorityContainer              priority_container = 1;
  TrafficLightStateInformation   traffic_light_state_information = 2;
  TrafficLightTimingInformation  traffic_light_timing_information = 3;
  TrafficLightSpeedAdvice        traffic_light_speed_advice = 4;
  TrafficLightInformation        traffic_light_info = 5;
}

docs.title: Priority container
docs.text:
message PriorityContainer {
  string   status = 1;     // Priority request status (see Use cases)
  Maneuver maneuver = 2;   // Direction for which priority is requested
  int32    lane_id = 3;    // Lane for which priority is requested
}

docs.title: Traffic light states
docs.text: State Description RED Red AMBER Amber GREEN Green ORANGE_FLASHING Orange flashing DARK Dark NO_LIGHT Lane without traffic light

docs.title: Traffic light timing
docs.text:
message TrafficLightTimingInformation {
  google.protobuf.Timestamp min_end_time = 1;   // Earliest possible phase change
  google.protobuf.Timestamp max_end_time = 2;   // Latest possible phase change
  google.protobuf.Timestamp likely_time = 3;    // Most likely phase change time
}

docs.title: Lane info
docs.text:
message LaneInfo {
  int32             max_lane_id = 1;  // Total number of lanes
  int32             lane_id = 2;      // Lane number (left to right, starting at 1)
  repeated Maneuver maneuvers = 3;    // Possible maneuvers for this lane
}

docs.title: Maneuver
docs.text:
message Maneuver {
  repeated Direction direction = 1;  // Possible directions: STRAIGHT, LEFT, RIGHT, U_TURN
  bool always_yield = 2;            // Whether to always give priority to intersecting traffic
}

docs.title: Error message
docs.text:
message ErrorMessage {
  ErrorType     error_type = 1;
  string        error_message = 2;       // Error details
  string        related_field = 3;       // Field that caused the error
  FmsItsMessage related_message = 4;     // Original message
  bytes         related_raw_message = 5; // Raw bytes if parsing failed
}

docs.title: Measurement units
docs.text:
enum MeasurementUnit {
  UNKNOWN = 0;
  KILOMETERS_PER_HOUR = 10;
  METERS_PER_SECOND = 11;
  KILOGRAM = 20;
  POUND = 21;
  METER = 30;
  CENTIMETER = 31;
  MILLISECOND = 40;
  SECOND = 41;
  MINUTE = 42;
  HOUR = 43;
  DEGREES = 50;  // range [0, 360)
}

docs.title: ITS event codes
docs.text: See Event codes for the full list with availability status.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text:
The REST API is based on the Open Trip Model 5.0 and is used to exchange vehicle and route information. All requests and responses use JSON over HTTPS.

All requests require a Bearer token in the Authorization header. See Authentication for details.

docs.title: Vehicle announcement
docs.text: Register a vehicle that will connect to our platform. This must be done at least every 24 hours to keep the vehicle active.

docs.title: Create or update vehicle
docs.text: PUT /vehicles

docs.title: Request body
docs.text:
{
  "id": "vehicle-123",
  "name": "Delivery Truck",
  "vehicleType": "truck",
  "licensePlate": "AB-123-CD",
  "fuel": "diesel",
  "externalAttributes": {
    "iVRIPriorityEnabled": false,
    "dynamicRate": false
  }
}
Field Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier for this vehicle (valid for 24 hours) name string No Display name for the vehicle vehicleType string Yes Vehicle type (see vehicle types) licensePlate string No License plate number fuel string Yes Fuel type (see fuel types) externalAttributes object No Extended properties for this interface externalAttributes.iVRIPriorityEnabled boolean No Set to true to activate iVRI priority requests for this vehicle externalAttributes.dynamicRate boolean No Set to true for dynamic location update intervals, false for fixed 1 Hz updates

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
200 OK - Returns the vehicle object as confirmed by the server.

{
  "id": "vehicle-123",
  "name": "Delivery Truck",
  "vehicleType": "truck",
  "licensePlate": "AB-123-CD",
  "fuel": "diesel",
  "externalAttributes": {
    "iVRIPriorityEnabled": false,
    "dynamicRate": false
  }
}

docs.title: Get vehicle
docs.text:
GET /vehicles/{id}

Returns the current vehicle announcement for the given ID.

200 OK - Vehicle found and returned.

404 Not Found - Vehicle not found.

docs.text: Value Description lightTruck Light truck boxtruck Box truck truck Truck heavyTruck Heavy truck trailer Trailer specialTransport Special transport dangerousGoods Dangerous goods bus Bus tram Tram pedestrian Pedestrian cyclist Cyclist moped Moped motorcycle Motorcycle car Car passengerCar Passenger car roadWork Road work vehicle rescue Rescue vehicle emergency Emergency vehicle safetyCar Safety car agriculture Agricultural vehicle military Military vehicle roadOperator Road operator taxi Taxi

docs.text: Value petrol diesel electricity hydrogen lng cng adBlue other

docs.title: Route announcement
docs.text: Register a route for a vehicle. This is mandatory when iVRI priority is enabled (iVRIPriorityEnabled: true), and recommended for all other use cases as it enables us to provide route-specific events earlier.

docs.title: Create or update route
docs.text: PUT /routes

docs.title: Request body (lat/lon array)
docs.text:
{
  "id": "route-456",
  "name": "Amsterdam to Rotterdam",
  "geoReferences": {
    "type": "latLonArrayGeoReference",
    "points": [
      { "lat": 52.3676, "lon": 4.9041 },
      { "lat": 52.0799, "lon": 4.3113 },
      { "lat": 51.9225, "lon": 4.4792 }
    ]
  },
  "actors": [
    {
      "associationType": "reference",
      "uuid": "vehicle-123",
      "entityType": "vehicle"
    }
  ],
  "actions": [
    {
      "associationType": "inline",
      "entity": {
        "actionType": "genericAction",
        "startTime": "2026-10-19T08:00:00Z",
        "endTime": "2026-10-19T17:00:00Z"
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Request body (address)
docs.text:
{
  "id": "route-789",
  "name": "Delivery to warehouse",
  "geoReferences": {
    "type": "addressGeoReference",
    "name": "Warehouse Rotterdam",
    "street": "Havenstraat",
    "houseNumber": "10",
    "postalCode": "3011 AB",
    "city": "Rotterdam",
    "country": "Netherlands"
  },
  "actors": [
    {
      "associationType": "reference",
      "uuid": "vehicle-123",
      "entityType": "vehicle"
    }
  ]
}
Field Type Required Description id string Yes Unique identifier for this route name string No Display name for the route geoReferences object Yes Geographic representation (see geo reference types) actors array Yes Exactly one actor linking the route to a vehicle actors[].associationType string Yes Must be reference actors[].uuid string Yes The vehicle ID this route belongs to actors[].entityType string Yes Must be vehicle actions array No Optional time window for the route actions[].associationType string No Must be inline if provided actions[].entity.actionType string Yes Must be genericAction actions[].entity.startTime string Yes ISO 8601 timestamp actions[].entity.endTime string Yes ISO 8601 timestamp (must be in the future)

Route lifecycle

  • A route is stored for 12 hours by default, unless startTime and endTime are specified
  • Submitting a new route for a vehicle that already has an active route will automatically replace the existing route
  • Only one active route per vehicle is allowed at any time
  • The vehicle referenced by actors[].uuid must be announced first

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
200 OK - Returns the route object. Note that the response uses geoReference (singular) rather than geoReferences.

{
  "id": "route-456",
  "name": "Amsterdam to Rotterdam",
  "creationDate": "2026-10-19T08:30:00Z",
  "lastModified": "2026-10-19T08:30:00Z",
  "geoReference": {
    "type": "latLonArrayGeoReference",
    "points": [
      { "lat": 52.3676, "lon": 4.9041 },
      { "lat": 52.0799, "lon": 4.3113 },
      { "lat": 51.9225, "lon": 4.4792 }
    ]
  },
  "actors": [
    {
      "associationType": "reference",
      "uuid": "vehicle-123",
      "entityType": "vehicle"
    }
  ],
  "actions": [
    {
      "associationType": "inline",
      "entity": {
        "actionType": "genericAction",
        "startTime": "2026-10-19T08:00:00Z",
        "endTime": "2026-10-19T17:00:00Z"
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Get route
docs.text:
GET /routes/{id}

Returns the current route for the given ID.

docs.title: Delete route
docs.text:
DELETE /routes/{id}

Removes a route. Returns 200 OK on success.

Tip

You can explicitly delete a route that is no longer needed, but submitting a new route via PUT /routes will also automatically replace any existing active route for the same vehicle.

docs.title: Geo reference types
docs.text: Three geo reference types are supported:

docs.title: latLonArrayGeoReference (preferred)
docs.text: An array of latitude/longitude points defining the route polyline. At least two points (start and end) are required. The more detailed the route, the more accurately we can provide route-specific events.

docs.title: latLonPointGeoReference
docs.text: A single latitude/longitude point. Requires lat and lon fields.

docs.title: addressGeoReference
docs.text:
An address-based reference. When used, we will determine the route coordinates. When only one address is provided, it is assumed to be the destination.

Field Type Required name string Yes street string No houseNumber string No houseNumberAddition string No postalCode string No city string No country string No

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
All error responses are returned as JSON:

{
  "code": "invalidField",
  "message": "Invalid value 'xyz'. Allowed values: [truck, bus, ...]"
}

Validation errors may return an array of errors:

[
  {
    "code": "missingField",
    "message": "Field 'vehicleType' is required"
  },
  {
    "code": "invalidField",
    "message": "Invalid value 'xyz' for field 'fuel'"
  }
]
HTTP Status Description 200 Success 400 Validation error or precondition not met 401 Unauthorized - invalid or missing Bearer token 403 Forbidden - vehicle has no features enabled 404 Resource not found 500 Internal server error Error Code Description missingField A required field is missing invalidField A field has an invalid value invalidRequest Request-level validation failure invalidJson JSON parsing error recordNotFound Resource does not exist PRE_CONDITION_NOT_MET Business rule violation (e.g., vehicle not announced before route)

docs.title: First-time connection
docs.text:
When an FMS connects for the first time, the vehicle information must be registered via the REST API before opening a WebSocket connection.

If priority use cases are desired, route information must be provided before the trip starts. For other use cases, providing route information is recommended as it enables us to provide events earlier.

docs.title: Regular position flow (position driven)
docs.text:
In position-driven event matching, events are checked each time a location update is received.

The FMS party must provide a location update at least once every 5 seconds (0.2 Hz) for each active vehicle. Based on this location, we check for new, updated, or deleted events and send them over the WebSocket.

docs.title: Regular position flow (event driven)
docs.text: In event-driven matching, events are matched based on the last known or calculated position.

docs.title: iVRI priority flow
docs.text: Precondition: Route must be registered via PUT /routes before the trip starts.

docs.title: Priority characteristics changed
docs.text: When vehicle characteristics change (e.g., entering/leaving an area where priority is applicable), the FMS must update the priority state.

docs.title: Unhappy flow: route tracking failed
docs.text: If a vehicle deviates from its route for too long, priority functionality may fail. The FMS party is notified through a control message.

docs.title: Unhappy flow: disconnect
docs.text:
In case of disconnection, the recovery depends on how long the connection has been down:

Scenario Action required Reconnect within 24 hours Only reconnect the WebSocket Reconnect after 24 hours Re-submit vehicle and route via REST API, then reconnect WebSocket

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text: This page describes the currently supported use cases in detail.

docs.title: Priority at traffic lights
docs.text:
To request priority at a smart traffic light (iVRI), it is mandatory that the route of the vehicle is known. We send priority requests in advance to traffic lights along the route.

We may choose to buffer priority responses of downstream traffic lights. In this case, only the latest status of the priority request for the traffic light the vehicle is currently approaching will be sent.

docs.title: Priority status flow
docs.text:
The normal flow of priority status values:

  1. requested - Priority request was detected by the traffic controller
  2. processing - Request is in queue, other requests are prior
  3. granted - Prioritization is active
  4. cancelled - Priority information should no longer be displayed

docs.title: Status values from Dutch SSM Profile
docs.text:
Status Description unknown Unknown state requested Request detected by the traffic controller processing Checking request (other requests are prior) watchOtherTraffic Cannot give full permission, watch for other traffic granted Prioritization is active rejected Request was rejected by the traffic controller maxPresence Request has exceeded max presence time reserviceLocked Reservice locked, controller requires time before accepting another request

For latest details, check CROW.

docs.title: Additional status values
docs.text:
Status Description cancelled After passing the stop line noAnswer No response from iVRI within 1 second wrongSeqNo Wrong response from iVRI (sequence number incorrect) maxEtaExceeded ETA missing or more than 5 minutes in the future noRoute Cannot find matching route noPbcMatch No configuration for route and vehicle

Note

Failed priority requests do not result in error messages. The reason is communicated through the status field.

docs.title: Traffic light status and timing
docs.text: We send traffic light status and timing information for traffic lights along the vehicle's route.

docs.title: Traffic light status
docs.text:
Each message indicates the current state of a traffic light for a specific lane:

State Description RED Red AMBER Amber GREEN Green ORANGE_FLASHING Orange flashing DARK Dark NO_LIGHT Lane without traffic light

docs.title: Traffic light timing
docs.text:
Timing information indicates when the traffic light state is expected to change:

  • min_end_time - Earliest possible phase change
  • max_end_time - Latest possible phase change
  • likely_time - Most likely phase change time (between min and max, relevant for traffic-actuated control)

Info

The iVRI container is transmitted when a significant change occurs. Without change, the message is transmitted every 10 seconds.

docs.title: Lane configuration
docs.text:
Per lane, an ITS event message with information from the variable message sign is sent. The nearest upstream sign (behind the vehicle) defines the current maximum speed and allowed lanes. Downstream signs (in front of the vehicle) allow anticipating upcoming changes.

  • Variable message sign information is not sent if all signs are blank
  • Lane numbers are counted left to right
  • The maximum speed value is what is displayed on the variable message sign (not the vehicle-specific maximum speed)

docs.title: Road configuration status values
docs.text: Status Description OPEN Open (falling green arrow) CLOSED / CLOSED_FOR_ALL_TRAFFIC Closed for all traffic (red cross) MERGE_RIGHT Merge right MERGE_LEFT Merge left END_OF_RESTRICTIONS End of restrictions CLOSED_FOR_YOU Closed for your vehicle type CHANGED_MAX_SPEED Temporary speed change BLANK Variable message sign is off

docs.title: Emergency vehicle approaching
docs.text: When an emergency vehicle is approaching, we send an EMERGENCY_VEHICLE_APPROACHING event. The event includes dynamic metadata with the speed and heading of the emergency vehicle, allowing the FMS to alert the driver in time.

docs.title: Dynamic sampling
docs.text:
When dynamicRate is enabled on the vehicle, we dynamically adjust the location update frequency by sending CHANGED_FREQUENCY_REQUEST events:

  • Intervals range between 1 and 60 seconds
  • The FMS party is allowed to send updates more frequently, but updates within 100ms of the last processed update will be discarded
  • It is advisable to send an additional location update when the vehicle speed changes significantly (more than 15 km/h since the last update)

docs.title: WebSocket interface
docs.text: The WebSocket interface is used for all real-time, bidirectional communication. Messages are encoded using Protocol Buffers (proto3).

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
Connect to the WebSocket endpoint at {baseUrl}/ws using the same Bearer token as for the REST API. Each vehicle requires its own WebSocket connection.

wss://{baseUrl}/ws
Authorization: Bearer <api_key>

TLS 1.3 is used for encryption.

Inactivity timeout

If no activity is detected on an open WebSocket during 5 minutes, the connection will be closed.

docs.title: Why Protocol Buffers?
docs.text:
The dynamic data exchanged over the WebSocket has high-frequency, low-latency requirements. Protocol Buffers provide:

  • Compact serialization (reducing bandwidth)
  • Cross-platform code generation (C#, C++, Java, JavaScript, Python, and others)
  • Extensibility

Use the protobuf runtime library for your development environment to parse incoming messages and serialize outgoing messages.

docs.title: Message structure
docs.text:
All WebSocket communication uses a single envelope message format (FmsItsMessage) containing three fields:

Field Type Description messageType enum The type of message vehicleId string The vehicle this message relates to container object The message payload

docs.title: Message types
docs.text: Type Direction Description LOCATION_UPDATE FMS → CSP Vehicle position, heading, and speed TIMESTAMP_MESSAGE Bidirectional Time synchronization EVENT_MESSAGE CSP → FMS ITS event information (traffic, priority, etc.) ERROR_MESSAGE CSP → FMS Error notifications

docs.title: Container contents
docs.text:
The container field holds different data depending on the message type:

Message type Container field LOCATION_UPDATE locationUpdateEvent TIMESTAMP_MESSAGE timestampMessage EVENT_MESSAGE infoContainer + contentContainer ERROR_MESSAGE errorMessage

docs.title: Location updates
docs.text:
The FMS party must send location updates for each vehicle over its WebSocket connection. Updates must be sent as a stream (not batched) to support real-time C-ITS services.

Default rate: At least 1 update every 5 seconds (0.2 Hz).

When approaching an iVRI, we may request higher frequency updates (up to 1 Hz) via a changed frequency request if dynamicRate is enabled.

Each location update should include:

  • Latitude and longitude
  • Heading (degrees)
  • Speed
  • GPS timestamp
  • Device timestamp (local clock at time of GPS fix)
  • GPS quality (deviation in meters, 95% probability)

GPS accuracy

GPS quality is crucial for accurate event matching. For the iVRI priority use case, we must be able to map coordinates to the planned route. Too much deviation will prevent priority requests.

docs.title: Time synchronization
docs.text: We regularly send timestamp requests (typically every minute) to verify clock synchronization. The FMS party must respond as quickly as possible.

docs.title: Timestamp request (CSP → FMS)
docs.text:
Contains:

  • requestTransmission - timestamp when we sent the request

docs.title: Timestamp response (FMS → CSP)
docs.text:
Contains:

  • requestTransmission - copied from the request
  • requestReception - timestamp when the FMS received the request
  • responseTransmission - timestamp when the FMS sends the response

Warning

If the average time difference consistently exceeds 3 seconds, or no response is received within 3 seconds, an error message will be sent.

docs.title: Event messages
docs.text:
We send ITS event messages containing traffic and infrastructure information relevant to the vehicle's current location and route. Each event message contains:

  • Info container - General metadata about the message (not event-specific)
  • Content container - The actual event data, varying by event type

Currently supported events: CHANGED_FREQUENCY_REQUEST, LANE_CONFIGURATION, PRIORITY, TRAFFIC_LIGHT_STATUS, TRAFFIC_LIGHT_TIMING, EMERGENCY_VEHICLE_APPROACHING. See Event codes for details.

docs.title: Error messages
docs.text:
Error messages are sent to the FMS party when issues are detected.

Error type Description ERRORTYPE_UNKNOWN Unknown error MISSING_FIELD An expected field is missing INVALID_FIELD A field has an invalid/unsupported value PRE_CONDITION_NOT_MET Required information via the REST API was not provided DATA_RATE_ERROR Location updates not being received according to specification NO_TIMESTAMP_ANSWER Timestamp response not received within expected timeframe TIMEDIFF_TOO_BIG Clock difference between FMS and CSP is too large INVALID_PROTO Protobuf message could not be decoded

docs.title: Reconnection
docs.text:
In case of disconnection:

  • Within 24 hours of vehicle registration: only reconnect the WebSocket
  • After 24 hours: re-submit vehicle and route information via the REST API before reconnecting the WebSocket
